# Sampled adversarial re-audit — reading the disagreement rate

The `SampledAuditLoop` re-audits a governed sample of already-merged PRs with a
fresh-context auditor that is never shown the original gauntlet verdicts. That
exclusion is the whole point: if the auditor saw "plan review approved, spec
review compliant, quality green" it would anchor on those verdicts and the
agreement rate would measure obedience rather than escaped defects. Each pass
appends one row to `audit_samples.jsonl` carrying the verdict plus the
`input_sources` manifest (`merged-diff`, `linked-spec-or-issue`, `repo-state`),
so "the auditor saw no verdicts" is verifiable straight from the record instead
of being a claim about the code.

Two numbers come out of the loop and they are easy to confuse:

- The **disagreement rate** — how often the fresh auditor refuses to
  rubber-stamp a merge. This is a rate over sampled merges, and the governor
  moves the sampling rate around the base rate in response to it (Shewhart
  control, one observation per tick recording the count and the sample size).
- The **escape rate** — how often a disagreement survives adjudication. Only
  upheld disagreements are real escapes; they cross-link into the escape ledger
  with `detection_source: sampled-audit`. Refuted ones are auditor false alarms
  and are charged against the false-alarm budget instead.

Gotcha seen on 2026-07-19: a malformed auditor response collapses to `agree`
with the raw text kept as findings. That is deliberate fail-soft behavior — a
parse failure must never be counted as a disagreement, because that would
inflate the headline bound and, through the governor, raise the sampling rate
on the strength of a JSON typo. When the disagreement rate jumps, check the
parse failures before believing the number.

Operational consequence: the ledger is the only place upheld escapes exist. As
of the 2026-07-19 host it holds 41 rows, 17 of them from the sampled audit, and
nothing in the dashboard reads them (see #9812).
